newsitem.title: MEXICO: Candidate attacked ahead of Mexico local elections.
newsitem.headline: Candidate attacked ahead of Mexico local elections.

text.p: Unknown assailants threw paint thinner in the face of the ruling party's mayoral candidate for the city of Cuernavaca and broke her nose, three days before municipal elections on Sunday, the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) said on Friday.

"Unidentified subjects who blocked her path threw a bottle of paint thinner in the face of the PRI candidate," a statement by the PRI said. It said her nose was broken and she was rushed to a hospital for emergency surgery.
The attack occured late on Thursday as the candidate, Ana Laura Ortega, walked with her husband in Cuernavaca, the capital of the state of Morelos, about 25 miles (40 km) south of Mexico City.
Voters in the rural state will elect mayors and a state legislature on Sunday, and polls have given Ortega a fighting chance in Cuernavaca in what is expected to be a tight race.

The PRI has ruled Mexico for 68 years, but has suffered setbacks in the last two years after an economic crisis ravaged Mexico. Inter-party violence often accompanies elections in Mexico, with the PRI and opposition parties blaming each other for the flare-ups.
The PRI said a Morelos senator had his jaw broken this week when assailants threw an aerosol spraypaint can at him. It suggested both events may have been related.
